content.title: ProfileImpl lifecycle: init, storage, deletion
content.description: Where a ProfileImpl instance is created, where ProfileManager keeps ownership of it, and where it gets destroyed.

notes.text: Class diagram of the ProfileImpl lifecycle, covering creation, storage, and

One level up: ProfileManager::GetProfile() first checks for an already-loaded profile, and if none exists, calls CreateAndInitializeProfile() with CreateProfileHelper bound as the synchronous creation callback.
ProfileManager asks Profile::CreateProfile() to build a new profile synchronously or asynchronously — this is the entry point into initialization.
Profile::CreateProfile() (defined in profile_impl.cc) sets up the profile directory and creation time before actually constructing the object.
This is the actual initialization point: `new ProfileImpl(...)` is constructed and immediately wrapped in a unique_ptr<Profile> for ownership.
ProfileImpl's constructor body — initializes path_, io_task_runner_, start_time_ and delegate_ before the rest of profile init runs.
Storage: profiles_info_ is the map that owns every loaded Profile object for the lifetime of the browser process — this is 'where it's stored' long-term.
RegisterOwnedProfile() inserts the freshly created profile (wrapped in a ProfileInfo) into profiles_info_, transferring ownership to ProfileManager.
One level up: UnloadProfileIfNoKeepAlive() calls UnloadProfile() once the profile's keep-alive refcount hits zero (e.g. last browser window closed) and kDestroyProfileOnBrowserClose is enabled.
Deletion trigger: UnloadProfile() erases the entry from profiles_info_. That drops the last unique_ptr owning the ProfileImpl, which destroys it synchronously.
ProfileImpl's destructor actually runs here — sends the destroyed notification and tears down pref observers, timers, and other owned state.
